name: The Bethesda System (TBS) for Reporting Cervical Cytology
specimen: Cervical/vaginal Pap smear – conventional and liquid-based (ThinPrep, SurePath)
use: All cervical and vaginal cytology specimens (screening and diagnostic), conventional or LBC.
Combined with HPV testing (co-testing/reflex) for risk-based management (ASCCP 2019).
not_use: Anal cytology – use the Bethesda terminology adapted for anal cytology (see Bethesda Anal).
Endometrial aspirates/brushings (no TBS categories – report descriptively).
report_structure: Specimen adequacy (satisfactory/unsatisfactory, with transformation zone and quality indicators)
General categorization (optional): NILM / Other / Epithelial cell abnormality
Ancillary testing (e.g. HPV) and automated review if used
Educational notes and comments (optional, consistent with guidelines)

adequacy.title: Satisfactory for evaluation
items: Conventional smear: estimated ≥8,000–12,000 well-preserved, well-visualised squamous cells.
Transformation zone (TZ) component: ≥10 well-preserved endocervical or squamous metaplastic cells (singly or in groups) – reported as present/absent, NOT a requirement for adequacy.
State quality indicators: partially obscured (50–75%), absence of TZ component, etc.

adequacy.title: Unsatisfactory for evaluation
items: Rejected/not processed: unlabelled specimen, broken slide, inadequate request.
Processed but unsatisfactory: inadequate squamous cellularity, or >75% of squamous cells obscured.
Any specimen with abnormal cells is satisfactory by definition.

adequacy.title: Special situations
items: Post-hysterectomy/vault and post-radiation/chemotherapy specimens may be judged on lower cellularity (≈2,000–5,000 cells) at the lab's discretion.
Bloody LBC samples: glacial acetic acid wash may salvage adequacy.

categories.name: Unsatisfactory for evaluation
categories.definition: Specimen cannot be reliably evaluated for epithelial abnormality. Either rejected/not processed (unlabelled, broken slide) or processed but unsatisfactory (cellularity or obscuring factors).
categories.management: Repeat cytology in 2–4 months (ASCCP 2019); if HPV co-test positive, colposcopy acceptable. Treat infection/atrophy before repeat if responsible.
criteria: Conventional smear: estimated <8,000–12,000 well-preserved, well-visualised squamous cells (use reference images; ≥5,000 not required to be counted).
Liquid-based: <5,000 well-visualised squamous cells (count fields at ×40/×10 per TBS table, at least 10 fields across diameter).
>75% of squamous cells obscured by blood, inflammation, thick areas, air-drying, contaminants (50–75% = satisfactory but partially obscured; mention as quality indicator).
Any specimen with abnormal cells (ASC-US or worse, AGC or worse) is by definition NOT unsatisfactory.
Rejected: unlabelled/mislabelled specimen, broken slide that cannot be repaired, inadequate requisition.

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – scant squamous cellularity
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but unsatisfactory for evaluation of epithelial abnormality because of scant squamous cellularity.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest repeat cervical cytology in 2–4 months. If HPV test was performed and positive, colposcopy is advised as per ASCCP 2019.

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – obscuring blood
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but more than 75% of squamous cells are obscured by blood.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest repeat sampling in 2–4 months, preferably avoiding menstruation; LBC may reduce obscuring blood.

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – obscuring inflammation
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but more than 75% of squamous cells are obscured by inflammatory exudate.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest clinical evaluation/treatment of any infection and repeat cytology in 2–4 months.

diagnoses.name: Unsatisfactory – air-drying / poor fixation / thick smear
diagnoses.final: Specimen adequacy: Unsatisfactory for evaluation – processed and examined, but unsatisfactory due to air-drying artefact / poor fixation / thick smearing involving most of the cells.
diagnoses.comment: Suggest repeat sampling with immediate fixation in 95% ethanol (conventional) or LBC vial.

diagnoses.name: Rejected – unlabelled / broken slide
diagnoses.final: Specimen rejected/not processed because of [unlabelled specimen / broken slide / mismatch with requisition].
diagnoses.comment: Please resubmit a correctly labelled specimen with a completed requisition form.

categories.name: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy
categories.definition: No cellular evidence of neoplasia. Organisms and other non-neoplastic findings are listed optionally.

rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

categories.management: Routine screening per age/HPV status. NILM + HPV-positive (non-16/18): repeat co-test in 1 year; HPV16/18 positive: colposcopy (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: Squamous cells: normal superficial/intermediate/parabasal with no nuclear atypia beyond reactive range.
May include organisms, reactive changes, atrophy, glandular cells post hysterectomy.
Transformation zone component (≥10 well-preserved endocervical or squamous metaplastic cells) is reported as a quality indicator, not an adequacy criterion.

diagnoses.name: Trichomonas vaginalis
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Trichomonas vaginalis.
diagnoses.comment: Pear-shaped flagellate organisms with eccentric nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasmic granules are seen. Suggest clinical correlation and treatment of patient and partner.

diagnoses.name: Fungal organisms morphologically consistent with Candida spp.
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Fungal organisms morphologically consistent with Candida spp.
diagnoses.comment: Pseudohyphae and yeast forms are seen, with 'shish-kebab' spearing of squamous cells. Suggest clinical correlation.

diagnoses.name: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Shift in flora suggestive of bacterial vaginosis.
diagnoses.comment: Clue cells (squamous cells covered by coccobacilli obscuring the cell border) with a filmy coccobacillary background and paucity of lactobacilli. Clinical correlation (Amsel/Nugent criteria) recommended.

diagnoses.name: Bacteria morphologically consistent with Actinomyces spp.
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Bacteria morphologically consistent with Actinomyces spp.
diagnoses.comment: Tangled clumps of filamentous organisms with acute-angle branching ('cotton-ball' / woolly bodies) are seen; usually associated with an intrauterine device. Suggest clinical correlation.

diagnoses.name: Cellular changes consistent with herpes simplex virus
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Cellular changes consistent with herpes simplex virus.
diagnoses.comment: Multinucleated cells with nuclear moulding, margination of chromatin and ground-glass nuclei (3 Ms), with occasional Cowdry A intranuclear inclusions. Suggest clinical correlation.

diagnoses.name: Cellular changes consistent with cytomegalovirus
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: Cellular changes consistent with cytomegalovirus.
diagnoses.comment: Enlarged (usually endocervical/glandular) cells with a single large intranuclear inclusion and halo, and small cytoplasmic inclusions. Rare; suggest clinical correlation, particularly immune status.

diagnoses.name: Other organisms (Chlamydia-suggestive changes, Leptothrix, Enterobius ova, Schistosoma ova, etc.)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Organisms: [specify, e.g. Leptothrix / Enterobius vermicularis ova / Schistosoma haematobium ova].
diagnoses.comment: TBS does not recommend a cytologic diagnosis of Chlamydia (nebular vacuoles are non-specific); advise NAAT if clinically suspected. Leptothrix often coexists with Trichomonas.
diagnoses.note: Listed in TBS atlas as other findings; not a separate formal TBS term.

diagnoses.name: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (includes typical repair)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive cellular changes associated with inflammation (includes typical repair).
diagnoses.comment: Mild nuclear enlargement with smooth membranes, fine chromatin and prominent nucleoli; repair shows flat cohesive sheets with streaming and no single atypical cells. Suggest treatment of cause and routine screening.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

diagnoses.name: Reactive cellular changes associated with radiation
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive cellular changes associated with radiation.
diagnoses.comment: Cellular and nuclear enlargement with preserved N:C ratio, bi/multinucleation, cytoplasmic vacuolation and polychromasia. History of radiotherapy noted; follow up as per oncology protocol.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

diagnoses.name: Reactive cellular changes associated with intrauterine contraceptive device (IUD)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive cellular changes associated with intrauterine contraceptive device.
diagnoses.comment: Small clusters of glandular cells with vacuolated cytoplasm and occasional single cells with high N:C ratio; history of IUD helps avoid over-interpretation as AGC/HSIL.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

diagnoses.name: Glandular cells status post hysterectomy
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Glandular cells status post hysterectomy.
diagnoses.comment: Benign-appearing glandular cells in a vaginal specimen after hysterectomy (e.g. adenosis, prolapsed tube, vaginal endometriosis). No further workup required.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings

diagnoses.name: Atrophy
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Atrophy.
diagnoses.comment: Predominantly parabasal cells in flat sheets with granular background, with or without inflammation ('atrophic vaginitis') or blue blobs. If atypia is equivocal, HPV testing or repeat after a short course of topical oestrogen may help.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings

diagnoses.name: Atrophic vaginitis (atrophy with inflammation)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Atrophy with inflammation (atrophic vaginitis).
diagnoses.comment: Parabasal cells, granular necrotic-looking background, neutrophils and degenerate/pseudokeratotic cells; not to be mistaken for tumour diathesis. Suggest clinical correlation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings

diagnoses.name: Keratotic changes (hyperkeratosis/parakeratosis) without atypia
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Squamous metaplasia / keratotic changes present.
diagnoses.comment: Anucleate squames and/or typical parakeratotic cells without nuclear atypia. May reflect prolapse or chronic irritation; correlate clinically.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Other non-neoplastic findings
diagnoses.note: Optional descriptor in TBS (non-neoplastic cellular variations).

diagnoses.name: Squamous metaplasia / tubal metaplasia
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).
diagnoses.comment: Benign metaplastic squamous cells (and/or ciliated tubal-type cells). Reporting of these non-neoplastic variations is optional.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Non-neoplastic cellular variations

diagnoses.name: Pregnancy-associated changes (decidual cells, Arias-Stella reaction)
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM).
diagnoses.comment: Decidual cells / Arias-Stella-type glandular cells consistent with pregnancy-related change. Clinical history of pregnancy supports a benign interpretation.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Non-neoplastic cellular variations

diagnoses.name: Lymphocytic (follicular) cervicitis
diagnoses.final: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM). Other non-neoplastic findings: Reactive changes – follicular cervicitis.
diagnoses.comment: Polymorphous lymphoid cells including tingible-body macrophages; may mimic HSIL or lymphoma. Seen in chronic infection (incl. Chlamydia) and in postmenopausal women.
diagnoses.cat: General categorization / Interpretation: NILM – Reactive cellular changes

categories.line: General categorization: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy

categories.name: Other: Endometrial cells (in a woman ≥45 years)
categories.definition: Benign-appearing exfoliated endometrial cells in a woman aged 45 years or older; TBS 2014 raised the reporting age from 40 to 45. Not reported in women <45 years.

rom.value: Not established in the sources reviewed
rom.source: No published series verified for this app (endometrial-cell risk varies with age and symptoms)

categories.management: Endometrial evaluation only if postmenopausal (or abnormal bleeding/risk factors); not needed for asymptomatic premenopausal women (ASCCP).
criteria: Small tight 3-D balls of cells with scant cytoplasm, small dark nuclei, sometimes with a stromal core ('exodus' pattern).
No atypia (if atypical → AGC, endometrial).
Menstrual status/hormone therapy should be stated where known.

diagnoses.name: Endometrial cells present in a woman ≥45 years
diagnoses.final: Other: Endometrial cells present in a woman ≥45 years of age. Negative for squamous intraepithelial lesion.
diagnoses.comment: Benign-appearing endometrial cells are present. Endometrial evaluation is recommended if the patient is postmenopausal or has abnormal uterine bleeding; correlate with menstrual history and hormone therapy.

diagnoses.name: Exfoliated endometrial stromal cells / histiocytes (≥45 y)
diagnoses.final: Other: Endometrial cells (stromal cells/histiocytes) present in a woman ≥45 years.
diagnoses.comment: TBS 2014 recommends not reporting isolated histiocytes; report only definite endometrial cells. Clinical correlation recommended.

categories.name: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance
categories.definition: Changes suggestive of LSIL that are qualitatively or quantitatively insufficient for a definitive interpretation.

rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

categories.management: Reflex HPV preferred. HPV-positive → colposcopy; HPV-negative → repeat co-test/HPV in 3 years (ASCCP 2019). Ages 21–24: repeat cytology at 1 year.
criteria: Nucleus 2.5–3× normal intermediate cell nucleus (≈35 µm²) or 2× squamous metaplastic nucleus.
Slightly increased N:C ratio, minimal hyperchromasia, mild irregularity of chromatin/nuclear outline.
Includes atypical parakeratosis and incomplete koilocytes.
Laboratory ASC:SIL ratio should be <3:1 (quality indicator); ASC rate typically ≤5%.

diagnoses.name: ASC-US
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US).
diagnoses.comment: Reflex high-risk HPV testing is recommended; management as per ASCCP 2019 risk-based guidelines.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-US – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance

diagnoses.name: ASC-US in atrophic smear
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US). Background atrophy.
diagnoses.comment: Atypia may be related to atrophy; HPV testing or repeat cytology after a course of topical oestrogen may help clarify.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-US – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance

diagnoses.name: ASC-US with atypical parakeratosis
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – ASC-US (atypical parakeratosis).
diagnoses.comment: Atypical parakeratotic cells with mildly enlarged dark nuclei. HPV testing recommended.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-US – Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance

categories.name: Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL
categories.definition: Changes suggestive of HSIL but insufficient for a definitive interpretation; usually small (metaplastic-size) cells.

rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

criteria: Small sparse cells, metaplastic size, nucleus 1.5–2.5× normal, high N:C ratio approaching HSIL.
Crowded sheet pattern: tight 3-D groups with loss of polarity in which HSIL cannot be confirmed.
Atypical repair, severe atrophy or post-radiation atypia where HSIL cannot be excluded.

diagnoses.name: ASC-H
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (ASC-H).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy and directed biopsy are recommended as per ASCCP 2019, irrespective of HPV status.
diagnoses.cat: ASC-H – Atypical squamous cells, cannot exclude HSIL

categories.name: Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
categories.definition: Encompasses HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1.

rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

categories.management: Colposcopy (HPV-positive or HPV not done); if HPV-negative, repeat co-test in 1 year acceptable (ASCCP 2019). Ages 21–24: repeat cytology at 1 year. Pregnancy: colposcopy may be deferred to postpartum.
criteria: Changes in mature (intermediate/superficial) squamous cells.
Nuclear enlargement ≥3× normal intermediate nucleus, hyperchromasia, irregular membranes, bi/multinucleation.
Koilocytes: sharply defined perinuclear cavitation with nuclear atypia (halo alone is not sufficient).
Keratinised cells with atypical nuclei can be LSIL.

diagnoses.name: LSIL (HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL), encompassing HPV cytopathic effect / mild dysplasia / CIN 1.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopic evaluation is recommended as per ASCCP 2019 risk-based management.

diagnoses.name: LSIL, cannot exclude HSIL (LSIL-H)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL); a few cells suspicious for HSIL are present (cannot exclude HSIL).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy recommended. Some laboratories use this optional qualifier; it is not a formal TBS category.
diagnoses.note: Non-TBS optional qualifier used by some labs; TBS discourages new categories.

categories.name: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
categories.definition: Encompasses moderate and severe dysplasia, CIS, CIN 2 and CIN 3. Option to add 'with features suspicious for invasion'.

rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

categories.management: Expedited treatment (LEEP) or colposcopy with biopsy (ASCCP 2019); expedited treatment preferred for non-pregnant ≥25 years when immediate CIN3+ risk ≥60%.
criteria: Smaller, less mature cells (parabasal/metaplastic) than LSIL; high N:C ratio.
Hyperchromasia, coarse chromatin, irregular nuclear contours with notches/grooves; nucleoli usually absent.
Single cells, sheets or hyperchromatic crowded groups (syncytial).
Features suspicious for invasion: tumour diathesis, macronucleoli, bizarre keratinised cells.

diagnoses.name: HSIL (moderate dysplasia / CIN 2)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), encompassing moderate dysplasia / CIN 2.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with biopsy or expedited treatment as per ASCCP 2019.

diagnoses.name: HSIL (severe dysplasia / CIS / CIN 3)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), encompassing severe dysplasia / carcinoma in situ / CIN 3.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with biopsy or expedited excisional treatment as per ASCCP 2019.

diagnoses.name: HSIL with features suspicious for invasion
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) with features suspicious for invasion.
diagnoses.comment: Tumour diathesis / features raising concern for invasion are present. Urgent colposcopy and biopsy are recommended.

diagnoses.name: HSIL involving endocervical glands (crowded groups)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL).
diagnoses.comment: HSIL cells are present in hyperchromatic crowded groups mimicking glandular lesions; flattening of cells at the periphery and absence of glandular features support HSIL with gland involvement.

categories.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
categories.definition: Malignant squamous neoplasm; TBS does not subclassify, but keratinising vs non-keratinising may be described.

rom.value: Grouped with HSIL+ in the ASCCP tables (immediate CIN3+ 25% HPV-neg / 49% HPV-pos); no separate SCC figure given
rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

categories.management: Urgent colposcopy/biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral.
criteria: Keratinising: pleomorphic single cells (caudate, tadpole, spindle) with orangeophilic cytoplasm, dense hyperchromatic/pyknotic nuclei; less diathesis.
Non-keratinising: syncytial aggregates of cells with coarse irregular chromatin, prominent nucleoli and tumour diathesis (granular necrotic debris, old blood).
LBC: diathesis clings to cell clusters ('clinging diathesis').

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma, keratinising type
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Squamous cell carcinoma (keratinising type).
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy, biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma, non-keratinising type
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Squamous cell carcinoma (non-keratinising type).
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy, biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.

diagnoses.name: Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Squamous cell – Squamous cell carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy and biopsy recommended.

categories.name: Atypical glandular cells
categories.definition: Glandular cells with nuclear atypia exceeding reactive/reparative change but lacking features of adenocarcinoma. Specify endocervical, endometrial or NOS; 'favor neoplastic' for endocervical or glandular NOS.

rom.source: Egemen D et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2020;24:132–143, Table 1A (KPNC, no known prior HPV result) – immediate CIN3+ risk, not ROM

rom.value: Histologic outcomes: HSIL 11.1%, AIS 2.9%, endometrial hyperplasia 1.4%, malignancy 5.2% (mostly endometrial); 71% benign
rom.source: Schnatz PF et al. Obstet Gynecol 2006 (systematic review, 24 studies, 3,890 AGC with histologic follow-up)

categories.management: AGC (all subtypes except atypical endometrial): colposcopy + endocervical sampling + endometrial sampling if ≥35 y or at risk. Atypical endometrial cells: endometrial and endocervical sampling first. AGC-favor neoplastic/AIS: diagnostic excision if no invasive disease (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: AGC endocervical NOS: sheets/strips with nuclear crowding, enlargement up to 3–5× normal endocervical nucleus, mild hyperchromasia, occasional nucleoli.
AGC endocervical, favor neoplastic: feathering/rosettes/strips but quantitatively or qualitatively short of AIS.
AGC endometrial: small groups, nuclei slightly enlarged, mild hyperchromasia, small nucleoli, ill-defined vacuolated cytoplasm.
AGC NOS: cell origin cannot be determined.

diagnoses.name: Atypical endocervical cells, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical endocervical cells, not otherwise specified (AGC, endocervical NOS).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with endocervical sampling (and endometrial sampling if ≥35 years or at risk) is recommended (ASCCP 2019).

diagnoses.name: Atypical endometrial cells, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical endometrial cells.
diagnoses.comment: Endometrial and endocervical sampling is recommended; colposcopy if no endometrial pathology is found (ASCCP 2019).

diagnoses.name: Atypical glandular cells, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical glandular cells, not otherwise specified (AGC NOS).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with endocervical sampling, plus endometrial sampling if ≥35 years or at risk, is recommended.

diagnoses.name: Atypical endocervical cells, favor neoplastic
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical endocervical cells, favor neoplastic.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy with endocervical sampling; if no invasive disease, a diagnostic excisional procedure is recommended (ASCCP 2019).

diagnoses.name: Atypical glandular cells, favor neoplastic
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Atypical glandular cells, favor neoplastic.
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy, endocervical and endometrial sampling; diagnostic excision if no invasive disease is identified.

categories.name: Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ

rom.value: High-grade lesion on histology in 91% (high-grade glandular lesion 88%)
rom.source: Roberts JM et al. J Low Genit Tract Dis 2005;9:71–77 (histologic follow-up of 67 cytologic AIS reports)

categories.management: Colposcopy, endocervical sampling and diagnostic excision (cold-knife cone preferred, intact specimen); hysterectomy after excision for most (ASCCP 2019).
criteria: Crowded sheets/strips with nuclear pseudostratification, feathering at edges, rosettes.
Enlarged elongated hyperchromatic nuclei, coarse even chromatin, mitoses and apoptotic bodies; nucleoli small or inconspicuous.
Clean background (no tumour diathesis).

diagnoses.name: Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS)
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Endocervical adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS).
diagnoses.comment: Colposcopy, endocervical sampling and diagnostic excisional procedure are recommended as per ASCCP 2019.

categories.name: Adenocarcinoma
categories.definition: Malignant glandular neoplasm; specify endocervical, endometrial, extrauterine or NOS when possible.

rom.value: Not established in the sources reviewed
rom.source: No published cytology-to-histology PPV series verified for this app

categories.management: Urgent gynaecological oncology referral; colposcopy/biopsy, endometrial sampling and imaging as appropriate.
criteria: Endocervical: abundant columnar cells in sheets/3-D clusters/single cells, enlarged pleomorphic nuclei, macronucleoli, tumour diathesis.
Endometrial: small 3-D clusters/single cells, nuclear size increasing with grade, prominent nucleoli, vacuolated cytoplasm, 'watery' finely granular diathesis, neutrophils within cytoplasm.
Extrauterine: clean background (no diathesis), papillary clusters/psammoma bodies (ovarian serous) or signet-ring cells (GI).

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, endocervical
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, endocervical.
diagnoses.comment: Urgent colposcopy/biopsy and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, endometrial
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, endometrial.
diagnoses.comment: Endometrial sampling and gynaecological oncology referral recommended.

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, extrauterine
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, extrauterine.
diagnoses.comment: Clean background suggests an extrauterine source (e.g. ovary, fallopian tube, GI tract, breast). Clinical and radiological evaluation for a primary is recommended.

diagnoses.name: Adenocarcinoma, NOS
diagnoses.final: Epithelial cell abnormality: Glandular cell – Adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified.
diagnoses.comment: Site of origin cannot be determined cytologically. Further clinical, colposcopic and endometrial evaluation is recommended.

categories.name: Other malignant neoplasms
categories.definition: Malignant neoplasms that are neither squamous nor glandular (specify).

rom.value: Not established in the sources reviewed
rom.source: No published series verified for this app

categories.management: Biopsy and ancillary studies; oncology referral.
criteria: Small cell / high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma: small cells with moulding, salt-and-pepper chromatin, crush artefact.
Carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Müllerian tumour), sarcomas, melanoma, lymphoma, metastatic tumours.
Cell block/IHC on residual LBC can help.

diagnoses.name: Small cell (high-grade neuroendocrine) carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells consistent with small cell (high-grade neuroendocrine) carcinoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biopsy with neuroendocrine IHC (synaptophysin, chromogranin, INSM1) recommended.

diagnoses.name: Carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Müllerian tumour)
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells with epithelial and spindle/sarcomatous components, suggestive of carcinosarcoma.
diagnoses.comment: Endometrial sampling and histological confirmation recommended.

diagnoses.name: Sarcoma (e.g. leiomyosarcoma, embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma)
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant spindle/round cells, suggestive of sarcoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biopsy with IHC recommended for classification.

diagnoses.name: Malignant melanoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells suggestive of melanoma.
diagnoses.comment: Melanin pigment / prominent nucleoli; confirm with S100/SOX10/HMB45/Melan-A on biopsy or cell block; exclude metastasis.

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Atypical lymphoid population suspicious for lymphoma.
diagnoses.comment: Biopsy with IHC/flow cytometry recommended; distinguish from follicular cervicitis.

diagnoses.name: Metastatic carcinoma
diagnoses.final: Other malignant neoplasm: Malignant cells consistent with metastatic carcinoma (specify likely primary if possible).
diagnoses.comment: Clinical history and IHC on biopsy/cell block are recommended to establish the primary site.

extra.title: HPV and management pointers (ASCCP 2019, risk-based)
items: Management is based on the patient's immediate and 5-year CIN3+ risk combining current result and history, not on cytology alone.
Primary HPV screening (FDA-approved assays) every 5 years from age 25 (ACS 2020) or co-testing every 5 years 30–65 / cytology every 3 years 21–29 (USPSTF).
HPV16/18 positive with NILM → colposcopy; other HR-HPV positive with NILM → 1-year repeat.
Use the ASCCP risk tables/app for individual decisions; WHO 2021 guidance favours HPV-DNA primary screening in low-resource settings.
